AI Weekly Digest
July 13, 2026
A few things worth knowing this week — here's what's happening in AI, in plain English.
TL;DR — Top picks this week
GPT-5.6 is now the preferred model in Microsoft 365 Copilot
Microsoft says its Copilot feature in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Chat and Cowork now runs on a newer AI model called GPT‑5.6. The upgrade promises faster and higher‑quality assistance, which could help you finish everyday tasks more efficiently.
OpenAI says GPT 5.6 is the ‘preferred model’ for Microsoft Copilot 365 amid breakup chatter
OpenAI confirms that its GPT‑5.6 model will continue to power Microsoft’s suite of workplace apps. This means the tools you already use for productivity will keep getting AI‑driven help, potentially improving how quickly and accurately you work.
Google will now disclose which ads are made with AI
Google will now require advertisers to label any ads that use AI‑generated or digitally altered content, expanding the rule beyond just political ads. If you manage marketing, you’ll need to make sure any AI‑created ads are clearly disclosed to stay compliant.
🧠 New Models
GPT-5.6 is now the preferred model in Microsoft 365 Copilot
Microsoft says its Copilot feature in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Chat and Cowork now runs on a newer AI model called GPT‑5.6. The upgrade promises faster and higher‑quality assistance, which could help you finish everyday tasks more efficiently.
Read more →
OpenAI says GPT 5.6 is the ‘preferred model’ for Microsoft Copilot 365 amid breakup chatter
OpenAI confirms that its GPT‑5.6 model will continue to power Microsoft’s suite of workplace apps. This means the tools you already use for productivity will keep getting AI‑driven help, potentially improving how quickly and accurately you work.
Read more →
Meta enters the crowded AI coding battle with Muse Spark 1.1
Meta has launched a new AI coding assistant called Muse Spark 1.1. It can automatically fix bugs, handle big coding projects, and move large codebases from one system to another. This could help our engineers work faster and reduce the time spent on repetitive coding tasks.
Read more →
🛠️ Tools & Products
ChatGPT is now a partner for your most ambitious work
ChatGPT Work is an AI assistant that can operate across your apps and files, stay on a project for as long as needed, and turn a goal into completed work. It could let you automate routine steps, giving you more time to focus on higher‑value activities.
Read more →
OpenAI is shutting down Atlas, but its AI browser ambitions are still growing
OpenAI is discontinuing its standalone AI web‑browsing tool, Atlas, after less than a year, but will keep some browsing features in its main desktop app and a Chrome extension. The change may affect how employees use AI to gather information online, while the remaining features could still help with research tasks.
Read more →
🏢 Industry & Adoption
Can AI answer the $3 trillion question?
There’s renewed debate about how much financial benefit AI can deliver, with estimates now reaching trillions of dollars and possibly big impacts. Understanding this potential return could guide how much your company invests in AI tools.
Read more →
Australian Payments Plus moves faster with ChatGPT and Codex
Australian Payments Plus is using paid versions of ChatGPT and a coding assistant called Codex to handle complex payment tasks more quickly while still relying on human oversight. It shows how AI can streamline routine finance work, suggesting similar tools could help our own finance or operations teams work faster.
Read more →
SK Hynix raises $26.5B in the biggest foreign IPO in US history, is urged to build new US fabs
SK Hynix raised $26.5 billion in a record U.S. stock offering and regulators are urging it and Samsung to build chip factories on U.S. soil. More domestic AI chips could improve the reliability of the hardware we depend on for AI projects and signals strong market interest in AI hardware.
Read more →
Hugging Face’s CEO on why companies are done renting their AI
Hugging Face runs a platform where companies can share and download free AI models and data, similar to how developers use GitHub for code, and about half of the Fortune 500 already use it. This offers a way to access AI tools without expensive licenses, potentially lowering costs for building AI solutions.
Read more →
🛡️ Safety & Policy
Google will now disclose which ads are made with AI
Google will now require advertisers to label any ads that use AI‑generated or digitally altered content, expanding the rule beyond just political ads. If you manage marketing, you’ll need to make sure any AI‑created ads are clearly disclosed to stay compliant.
Read more →
New York Times says OpenAI hid evidence in ChatGPT copyright trial
News publishers allege OpenAI kept hidden the tools and data that could show when ChatGPT reproduces copyrighted journalism, leading them to ask the court for penalties. This could affect how reliable AI-generated text is for our communications and may bring legal risks if we use such tools.
Read more →
How did the government decide OpenAI’s frontier model was safe to release?
A recent article points out that we don’t know exactly how the government talked to OpenAI and Anthropic about deciding whether OpenAI’s latest model was safe. This lack of transparency matters because it affects how much we can trust the safety of advanced AI tools we might consider using in the company.
Read more →
